Petitioner has filed instant writ petition seeking following relief :-

"10.1 That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly set aside the the impugned letter/order dated 05.06.2024 (Annexure P/1) whereby the representation the petitioner was rejected by the respondent authority and denied the annual increment from the date of suspension to rejoining, legitimate arrears of pay and allowances from suspension to rejoining and other legitimate benefits to the petitioner during the period of termination of his husband (late employee).

sentences.text: That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to call the records of the case from the respondent authorities.

10.3 That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue directions to the respondent to relies the annual increment from the date of suspension to rejoining,
legitimate arrears of pay and allowances from suspension to rejoining and other legitimate benefits to the petitioner during the period of termination of his husband (late employee).
10.4 That any other relief/order which may deem fit and just in the facts and circumstances of the case including award of the cost of the petition may be given."
3. Facts of the case in brief is that the husband of the petitioner was appointed as Panchayat Karmi at Gram Panchayat Kanki, P.S. Urga, District- Korba (C.G.) vide order dated 11/11/1995.
Later on he was declared as Secretary according to the provisions of Section 69 of the Panchayat Raj Adhiniyam.

In the month of February 2009 an FIR was registered against the husband of the petitioner for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420, 406, 409, 120(b) of IPC and he was arrested on 12/02/2009.
It is further pleaded that he was placed under suspension as he remained in judicial custody for considerable period.
The order of suspension has not been placed on record.
The husband of the petitioner was tried and he was acquitted of all the charges vide judgment dated 17/07/2018 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Korba.

The husband of the petitioner made a representation before the respondent No. 3 on 20/02/2019 for revocation of suspension order, but no decision was taken and on 10/02/2021 husband of the petitioner namely Shivnath Dhanwar passed away.
The petitioner being wife of the deceased moved an application for release of arrears of salary before the respondents No. 2 & 3 on 08/11/2021 but no action was taken.
4. The petitioner filed writ petition bearing W.P.(S) No.564/2024 claiming therein pending dues.

The writ petition was disposed of vide order dated 01/02/2024 granting liberty to the petitioner to make a representation before the respondent-authorities and in turn the authorities were directed to decide the representation.
The respondent No. 3 vide order dated 05/06/2024 rejected the representation and also denied annual increments from the date of suspension till date of death of husband of the petitioner.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would argue that husband of the petitioner was an employee of Panchayat Department, who was working on the post of Panchayat Secretary.
He would further argue that husband of the petitioner was not permitted to join services, as he was arrested in connection with criminal case, but no specific order of suspension was issued.

He would contend that it was informed by the respondent-authorities that husband of the petitioner was placed under suspension, therefore, an application was moved for revocation of suspension, when the husband of the petitioner got acquitted from the criminal case.
The husband of the petitioner namely Shivnath Dhanwar died on 10/02/2021 and till then no decision was taken on application moved by the deceased employee.

He would submit that as the husband of the petitioner was an employee of Panchayat, therefore, the fundamental rule, and other Civil Services Rules of State of Chhattisgarh for civil servants would not apply as specific rules have been framed governing the service of the Savita Dhanwar vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149523978/
2 Panchayat, namely C.G. Panchayat Service (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1999.

sentences.text: He would further contend that if the husband of the petitioner was placed under suspension, even then the petitioner would be entitled to get subsistence allowance from the date of suspension till his death.

He would submit that no show-cause-notice was issued to the husband of the petitioner till his death and no inquiry was conducted by the respondent-authorities according to the applicable service rules.
He would submit that though husband of the petitioner was placed under suspension but legally he was in service, therefore, he would be entitled to get subsistence allowance.
He would also submit that the subsistence allowance is not bounty and the employee or his legal heirs are entitled to get the amount of subsistence allowance.

He has placed reliance on the judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Capt. M. Paul Anthony vs Bharat Gold Mines Ltd. & Anr. reported in (1999) 3 SCC 679.
6.

entities.text: Capt. M. Paul Anthony vs Bharat Gold Mines Ltd. & Anr. reported in (1999) 3 SCC 679
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand Shri Khulesh Sahu, learned counsel appearing for respondents No. 3 & 4 would oppose the submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioner.

Shri Sahu vehemently argued that though the husband of the petitioner was an employee of Panchayat Department, but the provisions of Fundamental Rules would apply according to Section 69 of the Chhattisgarh Panchayat Raj Adhiniyam.
He would submit that the petitioner was notified as Secretary of Gram Panchayat by the State Government.
He would submit that CCA Rules as well as Fundamental Rules would apply.
He would contend that according to the provisions of Fundamental Rule 53 (4), an employee has to establish the fact that he was not gainfully employed during period of suspension.

He would submit that the petitioner failed to establish the fact that during suspension period her husband was not gainfully employed anywhere, therefore, the petitioner is not entitled to get arrears of subsistence allowance or salary.
He would contend that the husband of the petitioner was placed under suspension by the department and therefore an application was moved by the husband of the petitioner for revocation of suspension.
He would submit that the petitioner failed to place on record copy of order of suspension to demonstrate that he was placed under suspension.
He would further contend that the petitioner is not entitled to get arrears of subsistence allowance or salary.
7. Shri Sabyasachi Choubey, learned counsel appearing for the State would support the submissions made by Shri Sahu.

8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents.
9.
From perusal of the return filed by the respondents No. 3 & 4 it is quite apparent that husband of the petitioner was working as Panchayat Secretary under respondents No. 3 & 4.
It is nowhere stated that husband of the petitioner was not a Panchayat Secretary and he was not working with the department.
With regard to suspension, the respondents No. 3 & 4 have also not placed any document.
From pleadings it appear that on account of registration of a criminal case the husband of the petitioner was placed under suspension.
He was placed under suspension in the year 2009.

It is also evident from the documents filed by the petitioner as well as respondents No. 3 & 4 that no show-cause-notice was issued and no departmental inquiry was initiated against the husband of the petitioner during his life time.
The husband of the petitioner died on 10/02/2021 and till then he was in service.

Taking into consideration the documents placed on record and pleadings made in the petition and return it can safely be held that the husband of the petitioner was an employee of Savita Dhanwar vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149523978/

10. From pleadings made in the writ petition it is quite evident that the subsistence allowance was not paid to the husband of the petitioner during period of suspension, though he was entitled to receive subsistence allowance.
It is well settled principle of law that the subsistence allowance is right of government servant or employee of any institution or Board.
It is also held in catena of judgments by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that subsistence allowance is not bounty.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court dealing with the similar issue in case of Capt. M. Paul Anthony (supra) in paragraphs 27, 28, 29 and 30 held as under :-
"27.

The order of suspension does not put an end to an employee's service and he continues to be a member of the service though he is not permitted to work and is paid only subsistence allowance which is less than his salary, (See: State of M.P. v. of Maharashtra).
28.

entities.text: State of M.P. v. of Maharashtra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Service rules also usually provide for payment of salary at a reduced rate during the period of suspension.
(See: Fundamental Rule 53.)
This constitutes the "subsistence allowance".

If there is no provision in the rules applicable to a particular class of service for payment of salary at a reduced rate, the employer would be liable to pay full salary even during the period of suspension.
29. Exercise of right to suspend an employee may be justified on the facts of a particular case.
Instances, however, are not rare where officers have been found to be afflicted by a "suspension syndrome" and the employees have been found to be placed under suspension just for nothing.
It is their irritability rather than the employee's trivial lapse which has often resulted in suspension.
Suspension notwithstanding, non-payment of subsistence allowance is an inhuman act which has an unpropitious effect on the life of an employee.

When the employee is placed under suspension, he is demobilised and the salary is also paid to him at a reduced rate under the nickname of "subsistence allowance", so that the employee may sustain himself.

This Court, in O.P. Gupta v. Union of India made the following observations with regard to subsistence allowance: (SCC p. 340, para 15) "An order of suspension of a government servant does not put an end to his service under the Government.

entities.text: O.P. Gupta v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He continues to be a member of the service in spite of the order of suspension.

The real effect of suspension as explained by this Court in Khem Chand v. Union of India is that he continues to be a member of the government service but is not permitted to work and further during the period of suspension he is paid only some allowance generally called subsistence allowance which is normally less than the salary instead of the pay and allowances he would have been entitled to if he had not been suspended.

entities.text: Khem Chand v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no doubt that an order of suspension, unless the departmental enquiry is concluded within a reasonable time, affects a government servant injuriously.

The very expression 'subsistence allowance' has an undeniable penal Savita Dhanwar vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149523978/
4 significance.

entities.text: penal Savita Dhanwar vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The dictionary meaning of the word 'subsist' as given in Shorter Oxford 'English Dictionary, Vol. II at p. 2171 is 'to remain alive as on food; to continue to exist'.
'Subsistence' means means of supporting life, especially a minimum livelihood."
(emphasis supplied)
30. If, therefore, even that amount is not paid, then the very object of paying the reduced salary to the employee during the period of suspension would be frustrated.

The act of non-payment of subsistence allowance can be likened to slow-poisoning as the employee, if not permitted to sustain himself on account of non-payment of subsistence allowance, would gradually starve himself to death."
11.Now coming to the ground raised by counsel for the respondents No. 3 & 4 that the services of husband of the petitioner would be governed according to the provisions of Fundamental Rules.
The Fundamental Rule 2 states about extent of application.

It reads as under :-
"F.R.2. The Fundamental Rules apply, subject to the provisions of Rule 3 to all Government servants whose pay is debatable to Civil Estimates and to any other class of Government servants to which the President may by general or special order,
declare them to be applicable."
12. In Chhattisgarh Panchayat Raj Adhiniyam, rules have been framed governing the services of the department called as Chhattisgarh Panchayat Service (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1999.

entities.text: Chhattisgarh Panchayat Service (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1999
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Rule 1(3)
says that these rules will apply to all persons employed in connection with the affairs of Jila Panchayats, Janpad Panchayats and Gram Panchayats and discharging the function of these Panchayats.

Proviso to Rule 1(3) says that nothing in these rules shall apply to officers and servants of the State service who are posted under the Panchayat under Section 69 or on lone service to the Panchayat under Section 71 of the Panchayat Raj Adhiniyam.

As the husband of the petitioner was declared Secretary of Gram Panchayat according to the provision of Section 69 of the Adhiniyam,
therefore, these rules would not apply in the present case.

13. The husband of the petitioner was an employee of Panchayat Department, he was in service till his death and no inquiry was initiated against him during suspension period and no subsistence allowance was paid to the husband of the petitioner.
As no decision was taken on the representation made by the husband of the petitioner, therefore, the order Annexure-P/1 passed by the respondent No. 3 is hereby quashed.

The petitioner is permitted to make a representation before the respondent No. 3 within period of 10 days and in turn the authority concerned is directed to decide the representation preferably within a period of 45 days keeping in the mind the observations made hereinabove.
If it is found that the petitioner is entitled to get monetary benefits, the same shall be paid to the petitioner within next 30 days.
14. Accordingly, this writ petition is disposed of.
